resolve_schedule_prompt_template.value:
Convert the schedule description below into a standard 5-field cron expression: "minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week".

Rules:
- Respond with ONLY the cron expression, nothing else.
- The minute field MUST be a single literal number 0-59. Never "*", never a step like "*/5", never a list or range. Nothing may run more than once per hour.
- The hour field must be a single literal number 0-23, unless the description clearly asks for several specific times of day (then a comma list is allowed, e.g. "9,18").
- Prefer 9am (hour 9) when the description names a day or cadence but no time of day.
- If the description does not clearly describe a recurring time or cadence, respond with exactly: 0 9 * * *

Examples:
- "every day at 6pm" -> 0 18 * * *
- "every Sunday morning" -> 0 9 * * 0
- "the first of every month" -> 0 9 1 * *
- "every hour" -> 0 * * * *
- "9am and 6pm daily" -> 0 9,18 * * *
- "starting now" -> 0 9 * * *
- "remind me" -> 0 9 * * *

Description: "{description}"
resolve_schedule_prompt_template.description: Converts a free-text schedule description into a 5-field cron expression. Needs a {description} placeholder. Constrains output to once-per-hour minimum granularity (minute field must be a literal 0-59) and falls back to '0 9 * * *' when the text isn't clearly a recurring schedule - rewritten after a live incident where 'starting now' produced '* * * * *' (every minute). schedule_job.py's own schedule floor is the code-side backstop if the model still ignores this.

compose_generic_prompt_template.value: Write a short WhatsApp reminder message for this: "{description}". This is a self-chat with no name to address - never write "Hi [Name]" or any bracketed placeholder, and never invent a name. Do not invent specific details (like actual to-do items) that are not in the description itself - this is a nudge, not a report. If the description gives nothing concrete to say beyond itself, just restate it plainly instead of dressing it up with generic warmth.
compose_generic_prompt_template.description: Fallback reminder-message wording for anything Journal Agent doesn't cover. Needs a {description} placeholder. Rewritten after a live bug: the original ('warm... nudge') reliably produced unfilled "Hi [Name]" placeholders for content-free descriptions, since nothing ever told the model this is a self-chat with no name to fill in. run_routine.py's _looks_like_unfilled_template() is the backstop if this still slips through - the message is dropped rather than sent.
